forecast-period.text: A high pressure system centred over SA will weaken during Sunday. The tail end of a cold front will move across southern coasts early Monday then a high pressure system centred southwest of WA will extend a ridge across the south of SA. The main high centre will move to the east of SA late Thursday and Friday. A trough over the interior of WA will remain stationary for most of the week.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Patchy morning fog about the Mid North and Mount Lofty Ranges districts. Isolated light showers about the southern agricultural area, clearing late afternoon. Showers and isolated thunderstorms in the far west. Maximum temperatures mostly below average. South to southeasterly winds, fresh and gusty about northern parts during the day, tending east to northeasterly in the west.

Isolated light showers about the southern agricultural areas contracting to near southern coasts during the evening. Isolated showers and thunderstorms developing in the far west in the afternoon and evening. Southwest to southeasterly winds, tending east to northeasterly in the far northwest.

Morning fog patches about and east of the Mount Lofty Ranges. Possible early frost about the South East districts. Dry apart from showers and isolated thunderstorms in the far west. Maximum temperatures below average. Easterly winds becoming southwest to southeasterly during the afternoon and freshening near the coast, tending east to southeasterly in the west.

text.p: Dry apart from showers in the west and isolated thunderstorms in the far west. Maximum temperatures below average. South to southeasterly winds, fresh at times.

Cold at first about parts of central and eastern districts with patchy early frost. Dry apart from isolated showers in the far west. Maximum temperatures below average. Southeast to northeasterly winds, fresh at times.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Thursday: less than 2 mm about the southern agricultural area, although isolated falls of 2 to 5 mm are possible about the Mount Lofty Ranges, Kangaroo Island and the Lower South East. 5 to 15 mm is likely over areas west of about Ceduna but local heavier falls of 20 to 40 mm are possible nearer the western border with thunderstorms.
